subject: Request: onboarding stipend cap waiver & packaging clarification
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@brightforge.co>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: onboarding stipend ask + packaging question for BrightForge accelerator

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profile and token cost math. We run a 12-week accelerator and are finalizing the Redwood spot in our partner bundle. Two asks from our side that came up during committee review:

1) The standard onboarding stipend listed in the partner playbook is $5,000. Our cohort has a sponsored co-funding model and the operations team needs a slightly larger stipend to cover heavy first-month experimentation (~$9K). Is there any one-time flexibility on the stipend cap for sponsored accelerators?

2) We often convert promising pilots to dedicated capacity quickly. Is there a path to convert a portion of that stipend into a commitment credit (dedicated discount) within a 90-day window, and if so, what discount band applies?

Attached is a brief outline of cohort expected usage and sponsor coverage. Can you advise what exceptions/packaging you can offer, and any finance/legal steps to document it?

Appreciate it — we’re talking to two other providers so clarity here moves the needle.

Best,
Sam
Founder Partnerships
BrightForge Accelerator

Sam —

Thanks for the clear note and the cohort usage outline. Looping in Marissa (Partnerships) and Ben (Sales Ops) to evaluate. Two quick things from my side:

- We can consider an exception for sponsored accelerators, but need a short internal approval and a light MOU to capture sponsor obligations (who pays what, milestones).
- Converting stipend to a dedicated credit is feasible but requires a committed month-over-month minimum (we typically require a 6- or 12-month reserved commit to enable the discount).

Marissa/Ben — could you review the attached plan and propose a playbook option (one-time stipend increase vs milestone top-up vs conversion path)? If sponsor co-funds some portion that reduces Redwood liability, we can be more flexible.

I’ll hold off on a formal number until you both weigh in.

—Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Forwarding Sam’s ask — quick internal thread please.

On Wed, 29 Jul 2026 at 11:03, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sam —
>
> Thanks for the clear note and the cohort usage outline. Looping in Marissa (Partnerships) and Ben (Sales Ops) to evaluate...

--- internal notes ---

Marissa — my initial read: two pragmatic options that keep precedent low and sales traction high:

1) One-time uplift: increase onboarding stipend from $5k to $10k for this cohort, documented by a short MOU. No conversion rights; this is a grant.
2) Conversion window: keep stipend at $6k, but allow conversion of up to $4k into a dedicated credit if BrightForge signs a 6-month reserved commit within 90 days; conversion triggers a 20% discount on the committed spend for first 3 months (intro band).

Ben — which option is lighter from an ops and rev-rec perspective? If we do (2) we need a simple addendum capturing conversion mechanics and an approval from finance.

—Markus
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: onboarding stipend ask + packaging question for BrightForge accelerator

Agree we should be careful about precedent. Quick ops input:

- Option 1 (one-time uplift to $10k) is the simplest from billing/finance; we treat it as a grant/marketing expense and report as such.
- Option 2 (partial conversion) is doable but we need: (a) an explicit conversion clause, (b) a minimum reserved commit (I recommend 6 months at $2k/mo minimum), and (c) approval from RevRec/Finance for how credits map to committed revenue.

If the sponsor is willing to underwrite >= 40% of the uplift, we can go with Option 1 and avoid complicated accounting. If BrightForge wants conversion optionality, we should require a signed conversion addendum with clear milestone dates.

Numbers from the usage deck look like: month1 burst ~1.2M tokens, expected steady state 200-300k tokens/mo. With our hosted token price assumptions, the financial risk on a $10k stipend is acceptable if co-funded.

—Ben
Sales Operations
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: onboarding stipend ask + packaging question for BrightForge accelerator

Sam —

Appreciate the patience. After internal review we can offer a scoped concession to get BrightForge live quickly: 

Proposal (final):
- One-time onboarding uplift to $9,000 (paid as grant).
- Optional conversion clause: BrightForge may convert up to $4,000 of that uplift into dedicated-credit applied to a 6-month reserved commit if the commit is signed within 90 days of cohort start. Conversion will apply a 20% introductory discount to the converted amount for the first three months of the reservation.
- Sponsor co-funding: if your sponsor covers at least 40% of the uplift (~$3,600), Redwood will process the uplift immediately; otherwise Redwood will require a short MOU and finance approval cycle (3–5 business days).

Attached is a draft MOU capturing the uplift and conversion clause. If this looks good, please confirm sponsor commitment and I’ll route the MOU to legal and then to DocuSign.

Next steps:
1) Confirm sponsor co-funding (yes/no + amount).
2) If yes, return signed MOU or confirm and we’ll kick off DocuSign.
3) If no, let us know and we’ll start internal finance approval (3–5 business days).

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
